title: Open the job's PR early at verification start, with no email literals
summary: Retry the early-PR job: when verification starts in athena go, push the candidate and open or update the job's PR through the host seam without merging, so CI caches by fingerprint. Failures are non-fatal, a non-GitHub origin skips silently, land reuses the PR, and no email literal is written anywhere.

defaults_applied.how: New tests plus cargo test, clippy, and fmt clean.
No email or personal data written to files.
Criteria check pushes, PR opening, and outcome via the fake host.
One focused change to the early-PR step and its land reuse.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: Goal: speed up jobs by letting CI fill the fingerprint cache during verification; audience is the Athena maintainer and the verifier.
Retry keeps the earlier accepted reading (open or update the PR early, never merge, silent skip without GitHub origin, non-fatal failures) and adds the no-email-literal constraint.
No email literal is needed; PR creation uses the existing gh/git identity.
The deliverable list from the accepted earlier reading is reused.

acceptance_criteria.text: A fake-host test shows that when verification starts in Athena::go, the candidate is pushed to the job's PR branch and the PR is opened or updated via Remote::push and PrHost::open_pr before verification completes, with no merge call. Run: cargo test -p athena-core.
A fake-host test shows a failing early push or early open_pr leaves the job's outcome identical to the no-failure case (job does not fail; land proceeds as today). Run: cargo test -p athena-core.

A test shows land still pushes the landing commit to the same branch, reuses the early PR (no second open_pr), uses the lease-pinned replace via check_replace, sets link.head to the landing commit after the replace and before the head check, and merges guarded with the landing commit. Run: cargo test -p athena-core.

A test runs go with no origin or a non-GitHub origin and shows the early step is skipped silently: no output line contains 'warning'. Only a host error on a GitHub remote prints a warning. Run: cargo test --workspace.
cargo test --workspace, cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets, and cargo fmt --check all pass clean. Each new test fails without the new behavior.

The diff adds no email address literal to any source, test, or doc file; any identity comes from existing config or git settings, or an address already on the admission allow-list. The diff was scanned for emails before finishing.
The production early-push implementation builds its own GhCli runner, so the Athena::go signature and CLI call sites are unchanged.

CHANGELOG.md says verification start opens or updates the job's PR so CI caches by fingerprint, that it never merges, that a missing or non-GitHub origin is skipped quietly, and that failures are non-fatal.

out_of_scope: Changing the admission allow-list or adding a producer-loop email check
Changing merge behavior of athena land
Changing the Athena::go signature or CLI call sites
departures: Larger multi-file change touching the host seam and land reuse, so cost and time are above reference.
